task.pr_title: fix: detect closed pooled connection without consuming pending push data (RESP3 + hiredis) (#4128)

cases.provenance: A human reviewer flagged this defect in an inline comment on the reviewed pull request.
cases.description:
Could you also handle POLLRDHUP? 
Note it has to be added to the poller.register() mask, not just the returned-events check, or poll() won't report it.  Guard it with getattr(select, "POLLRDHUP", 0) so macOS/Windows keep relying on POLLHUP.
On Linux, a graceful peer close (FIN) reports POLLIN|POLLRDHUP, not POLLHUP, so _socket_is_closed() currently returns False and the stale connection is still reused. Current solution covers macOS/BSD (they set POLLHUP on FIN) but not Linux.

Also, the socketpair() tests use AF_UNIX, which sets POLLHUP on close just like macOS — so they pass even though the Linux TCP path isn't detected. Could you add a regression test that will cover this addition? That will fail on the current code and pass once POLLRDHUP is handled.

evidence.attached_diff_hunk:
@@ -52,6 +52,24 @@ def _socket_can_read(sock, timeout: float) -> bool:
         return bool(selector.select(timeout))
 
 
+def _socket_is_closed(sock) -> bool:
+    # A server-closed socket reads as ready (it yields EOF), so readiness alone
+    # cannot tell it apart from a socket holding pending data. poll() can:
+    # POLLHUP/POLLERR/POLLNVAL flag a closed/errored socket while a live socket
+    # with buffered data reports POLLIN only. Polling is non-destructive, so any
+    # pending push messages are left intact. Without poll() the two states are
+    # indistinguishable here, so report not-closed.
+    if not _HAS_POLL:
+        return False
+    poller = select.poll()
+    poller.register(sock, select.POLLIN)
+    events = poller.poll(0)
+    if not events:
+        return False
+    _, revents = events[0]
+    return bool(revents & (select.POLLHUP | select.POLLERR | select.POLLNVAL))
